# Rohiṇijātaka (Ja 45)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Rohiṇijātaka* (Ja 45) is a short narrative included in the Ekanipāta of the Pali Jātaka collection [Appleton 2010]. Set at Jetavana, the story was told by the Buddha concerning a maidservant named Rohiṇī in the employ of the merchant Anāthapiṇḍika [Fausböll 1877]. While Rohiṇī was pounding rice, her elderly mother lay down nearby and was tormented by flies; asking her daughter to drive them away, Rohiṇī took up a pestle and struck at the flies, inadvertently crushing her mother to death and bursting into lamentation [Fausböll 1877]. The Buddha revealed that this was not the first time she had done so, reciting the past story (*atītavatthu*) set during the reign of Brahmadatta in Bārāṇasī [Fausböll 1877]. In that past life, the Bodhisatta was born into a merchant family (*seṭṭhikula*), and his maidservant Rohiṇī killed her mother in identical circumstances [Fausböll 1877].

The central gāthā of the Jātaka (*Seyyo amitto medhāvī yañ-ce bālānukampako...*) observes that an intelligent enemy is preferable to a compassionate fool, pointing to the wretched Rohiṇī who killed her mother and then grieved [Anandajoti 2010; Fausböll 1877]. In the conclusion (*samodhāna*), the mother and daughter are identified with their previous counterparts, while the Buddha identifies himself as the wise treasurer of that time [Fausböll 1877]. The story appears in the chapter verse summary (*uddāna*) between the *Makasajātaka* (the mosquito story) and the *Ārāmadūsakajātaka* [Appleton 2010; Fausböll 1877].
